newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones to seek to have award set aside.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones to seek to have award set aside.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co said Thursday it would seek to have the judge set aside a $223 million award that a federal jury awarded a defunct securities firm for damages in a libel suit against Dow Jones.
"We will seek to have the judge set aside the award," Paul Steiger, managing editor of financial daily newspaper The Wall Street Journal, was quoted as saying in a statement released by the company.
"And we are optimistic, based on applicable law, that it will not stand."

The jury's decision followed a two-week trial in which Houston-based MMAR Group Inc said it was forced out of business by a critical, error-filled article published in October 1993 by the financial daily, whose publisher is Dow Jones.
The plaintiffs' attorneys said it was the biggest jury award ever in a libel case.
